utterances.text: You mentioned that your lap top didn't work and therefore you referred to page 30 in a rather vague way so I find it very attentive of the technicians to come to help you even if you do not explicitly ask for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am grateful to everyone, but it didn't work. There is a certain discrepancy with regard to the lines I just didn't mention this because I wanted to avoid losing track of the line one was referring to. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'd now like to go back to the issue of direct and indirect fire. You mentioned the form of these wounds and my question is as follows: Is it possible to always exclude or is it possible not to exclude the possibility of a ricochet when one examines a wound, and if it is possible or if it is not possible, what are the reasons for this?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: I said that when a projectile encounters an obstacle, then it's possible for it to ricochet. I also forgot to say that when a projectile hits a hard surface, the angle at which it rebounds from the hard surface is not as great as when the projectile rebounds after having hit a water surface. Why is this important? When a projectile hits a hard surface, a wall or wood, et cetera, then the projectile is deformed and the deformation at the front, at the tip of the projectile forms an irregular entry wound and it now has the impression of that projectile, an angle of the projectile at which the projectile hit a surface. If the projectile hits a surface but is damaged, let's say like this, horizontally, and it just catches a surface, it's not deformed at the front, it's possible for such a projectile to enter at a right angle or at some other angle and then the wound can be a regular wound as if the projectile was a regular one which didn't ricochet. So it's only if the tip of the projectile is deformed, having hit an obstacle. In such cases it causes an irregular wound but if the axis of the projectile hasn't been changed, if it hasn't been deformed at the tip, then the entry wound doesn't have other characteristics, it doesn't have characteristics that could distinguish it from the characteristics of a wound caused by a regular hit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, according to your answer, it's theoretically possible to find wounds which resemble wounds caused by a direct hit; is that what you wanted to say, that a wound caused by a ricochet can resemble a wound caused by a direct hit?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, is it also possible, since you are speaking about lateral deformation, is it possible to have deformations which are more significant on the projectile itself but by accident, it enters the body at a right angle and the entry wound can be compared to or similar to or what one calls a direct wound; is this possible?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: This is the projectile, let's say, what causes the diameter of the wound is this cross-section here. So if it enters like this and then the wound is circular so damage that might be caused here would not affect the entry wound but if the projectile, having hit an obstacle has the tip, the front part which is deformed then this will be the diameter of the projectile and then the wound will have more or less the same shape as the tip here. And about -- with regard to wounds, I should tell you the following immediately and this is why I say that it's always necessary to carry out an examination. The scars left on the skin caused by such wounds, they are also dependent on the size and the form, the shape of these entry wounds, when the projectile is a direct hit, these scars are relatively regular, provided that the doctor did not intervene. If the projectile caused an irregular wound, for example, as is the case in exit wounds, in that case, the scar will also be irregular and on the basis of the look of the scar, if we carry out the examination of someone who was wounded at an earlier date, we can determine the entry and exit wound and the trajectory and we can determine whether the projectile entered he had at a right angle or an in a regular manner or whether it entered in an irregular manner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Professor, thank you. When one describes a wound, and I'm referring to entry wounds, on the basis of your experience, can you tell us whether, according to the laws, the rules of the profession, must one -- should one describe this wound in precise physical terms, et cetera, or perhaps not?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: Well absolutely, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, with regard to all the information, all the exhibits you could examine with -- in relation to all the incidents that you looked into, was there a similar description, yes or no, a similar technical description of the entry wound that you came across in these documents?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, no. That's why I --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'll stop you there. You can finish later but I'll interrupt you now. At the time, was it possible to give a physical description and to say how these entry wounds appeared?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Professor, what, in technical terms, are the results, are the scientific results, of these omissions in all these documents of the fact that the description of the entry wound was not present in all these documents?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: Well, one of the results is I can't say whether it was a direct projectile, I can't tell you whether it's -- whether it concerns one projectile or a rifle projectile or whether it concerns some other kind of projectile. When I say some other kind of projectile, then I'm referring to a fragment of an obstacle hit by a projectile or perhaps a projectile that ricochetted, deformed projectile or -- a projectile can also be made of fragmentation matter, it goes very far and is not regular, that's also called a projectile and can inflict a wound too but on the basis of this description, these descriptions that I had in the medical documentation, it's impossible to come to such conclusions, even in the cases where we have a diagnosis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Professor, you've said that projectiles include several things. You spoke about and drew a certain number of what we would call bullets, what else would you include in this category, in the category of projectiles, as an expert, as a specialist in this field, what would you include in this category?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: Well, very broadly speaking, that would include any object that causes a sort of hole and has a channel. Do you want me to show you a photograph of a wound caused by shrapnel, caused by a projectile that disintegrated? I have this in colour, I have prepared this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spoke about the fragmentation of shells, do you include this in the category of projectiles that might have been involved in certain incidents? Given you that you don't have enough information, would you include these things in such a category in such a projectile category?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: Even a part of shrapnel is a projectile when it hits the body but I cannot define the wound from the documentation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, Professor, but is there a theoretical possibility or practical possibility that in the cases that you have examined, when the wound, for instance, had caused that death that there were projectiles that would have caused this death were not bullets as we call them but were other projectiles? Not bullets. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, I have understood the question but let me just think. I believe that there was a person, I don't remember what the incident number was, it was in the maxillary sinus that she was hit at and she had a -- it's a very thin body, there was a part of the projectile or a projectile or "projectile" had stopped at the maxillary sinus and according to the witness statement testimony, there was a gravel surface. We don't know whether that was a part of that surface which had been an actual projectile or it was part of the, say, fragmented jacket of the projectile we don't know that because I don't have the documentation that can tell us this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Professor?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: Are you speaking about incident number 17, to clarify things, could you please check if you can?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. And I have written it down not only examination has to be carried out but also an x-ray has to be taken to establish this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in a general sense, could it be that in all the cases that you have examined, apart from -- without having a precise definition of a type of wound, one wound which we would think was caused by a bullet, sometimes it could be caused by something else. Now this possibility, does it exist as long as we don't have the form and a full description of the wound?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: In these cases that I have mentioned where there is doubt because of the size of the wound or because of the damage that it caused, I don't know that. You're asking me something that I cannot answer also because of the medical documentation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well. But I'm going to ask the question differently now. Normally, would you need a medical file which would give you all the necessary elements to give such an answer, for instance, yes, bullet wound or to say no, wound caused by something else? Would you need such a medical file with all the elements? Very briefly.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: They would have to be found if everything was carried out that was supposed to be carried out by the doctor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. But in -- as far as you know, about your field of expertise, and about also the delicate circumstances at the time, do you think that this would have been technically achievable?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: Not only it should have been done, technically, that it was possible, but it should have been done first. The therapy, the treatment depends on the diagnosis, the diagnosis has to be established what had entered the body. You have to have an x-ray, you have to have an examination, you have to have all this in order to take some steps in terms of treatments so if this has been done, if this has been a medical intervention has followed all that had to have been noted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand what has to be done. The question, however, was whether, if you would have all data available, whether you could distinguish between a bullet wound and a wound of a different character such as, for example, caused by shrapnel pieces. Yes. That was the question, as far as I understood, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, that will be technically possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was the pre-question, Mr. President. The question in the -- in its second part is the following:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you have any idea, perhaps you do, perhaps you don't, that for what should have been done technically speaking, was not done? Do you have an opinion as to why this was not done?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know whether this last part of the question was properly translated. Could you please, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, repeat the last few words of your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course. The question is the following:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since, witness, you are telling us that certain things should have been done, and you're telling us that apparently they were not carried out, they are not in this file, do you have an opinion as a practitioner why, according to you, these things were not done?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it and then the objection stands, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're asking about why certain things that would be necessary to establish in order to be able to draw certain conclusions, whether it has not been done. Professor Dunjic, this question is a question why certain research is not done, a certain examination is -- some data are not available. The question is whether you know why this happened. Let me first of all ask you, do you have any factual knowledge of why it did not happen, so not in theory, but first of all, whether you know anything about it, why, in these cases, certain facts were not -- medical facts were not established.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no knowledge about why this was not done. Factual, no, I don't know, because that's not that has not been written here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would your field of expertise, could that give an answer to that question? Is the forensic medicine a field of expertise which could answer the question why a certain examination or certain data have not been collected?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Theoretically speaking, forensic medicine at the time involved in, among other things, also carries out an analysis of omissions done by the doctor and would look for the reasons why these omissions have been committed and in our law on -- our Criminal Code, there is something that there is -- when treatment has not been carried out properly. Now, what I've spoken about, our field, forensic pathology and so on. And then there is a second segment when we give our opinion why something was not done and should have been done. This belongs to another area that is covered by forensic medicine and that is a professional obligation that we have together with the clinical doctors who are involved in the treatment for certain areas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but just the question if -- well, let's say the entry bullet has not been properly described, does the -- your field of expertise give an explanation as why it has not been properly described, just give an example of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. So the witness testified that there is no factual knowledge, nor does his expertise allow him to answer this question. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, we have two other subjects to cover quickly but you spoke about incident number 11 or rather I want you to speak about incident number 11 and could you focus on what we call the medical documentation which is relevant for incident number 11?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: Let me just find it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you found the incident and the documents?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What can you tell us, very briefly, witness, about what we can think about this type of document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I don't know if we can put it on the ELMO, I believe that we can. This is documentation which is not under seal, is not protected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As you will understand, I do not know that by heart, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. You prepared for the examination of this witness so therefore I take that you checked it but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this is ERN00269827. I don't see an R which is a good sign. I believe that we can put it. Perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's just go into a private session for one second.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we just have a look at the document, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, so that we double-check.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Professor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Professor, here we are, we are going to have a look at this document and we would like to hear your comments in relation to this document. What does this document tell us, what does it not tell us, et cetera, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: This document you can see that it's a medical faculty of Sarajevo, Institute of Forensic Medicine. So this is the institution that issues this document on the 1st of March, 1995. So this is when this document was issued. We can see the name of the person, I'm not going to read it, and then it says he was born 1937 then it says the examination-autopsy 8th of September, 1993. And then it says the date of the incident, 7th of September, 1993. Then under four it says that there was a diagnosis established of the injuries and the cause of death. So that is a form and in the -- this space, it says DG, diagnosis, V, transsclopetarium, that is from a firearm, capitis, that is in the area of the head, regionis frontalis lateris dextri, in the frontal area of the -- on the right-hand side and then we have the signature of the person who has done this. From this document, we found out that the person in question was wounded not when this person died but when it was wounded on the 7th of September and it says on the 8th of September, I don't know whether this was an autopsy that was done on the 8th of September or that there was just an outside examination that was done. I don't know. From this diagnosis it says that this was a firearm injury in the in the right area of the top of the head, I cannot answer what type of projectile had caused the wound, whether this projectile stayed in the body or whether it went through the body. I cannot tell you anything about the size of the injury because there is no autopsy report, there is no description. I cannot tell you about the channel and the direction of the injury because there is no such a thing from an autopsy report. If I had all this then I would be able to say this person suffered such and such an injury one or more than one. Whether this was just an entry wound or was an entry and exit wound and none of the questions we discussed so far. We cannot tell anything even about the position of the body or the head in relation to the oncoming projectile. This projectile could have gone this way, that way, --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is -- I don't count it but approximately the 15th time or the 20th time that you have explained to us that if you have not sufficient data, that you cannot draw any conclusions. That point has been made 15 times now or 20 times. It's perfectly clear already from your report. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Professor, very briefly, if we are carrying out an autopsy, is it normal to keep a protocol of this or a record of this autopsy, an autopsy report -- in the autopsy report?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us very briefly what would such record have or be included in you can just tell us in a nutshell?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: All of this that I have spoken about so far, number of, type of injuries, cause of death and all the details that are necessary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And the document that we have just seen, can it or can it not correspond to such a record of an autopsy?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, we are going to change the subject now. We're going to examine the three elements that you have spoken --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I would like to, yes, I would like to have a break in five minutes. Could you conclude by then? I asked the Defence to conclude in approximately one hour it's now one hour and 20 minutes and even if some five, six or seven minutes were lost by sending the witness out, nevertheless it's considerably more. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, with the assistance of the witness, I will manage to do it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very briefly, witness, you have spoken to us about your experience in the field of suicides; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, in peace circumstances, what is the rate of suicide that you know in relation to 100 and then -- 100.000 inhabitants?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: In war --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: This is both irrelevant and is a subject matter that is outside the scope of the expertise of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness might have some knowledge about if you study patients of suicide, you might have some knowledge as to the frequency of -- I do not know, usually it takes more to send the witness out and let's show that it's relevant, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, within the next one or two questions or otherwise. Five minutes will be gone any how.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you please focus on my questions and just answer with a yes or no when it's possible. Do you know the rates of suicide in normal circumstances; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. What is the rate in normal circumstances for 100.000 inhabitants?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: I cannot give you in figures now an answer, but it is well-known that in normal circumstances --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you don't know, Professor, then I'm sorry just tell me that you don't know. I don't want to vex you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, with your leave, it depends from an area to another area. I'm speaking about peace circumstances, peace conditions as far as I understand that's what's important and in some extraordinary circumstances and because I have written a book about suicide, from 1920 until 1990, based on the autopsy material at the institute of forensic medicine I can answer that but --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but for the moment, I'm not talking about extraordinary circumstances, Professor, I'd just like a rate. If you have it, that's fine. If you don't, we'll just go on to another subject.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: This is what my answer is: The relation between murder and suicide is 1:5 that is in favour of a suicide. There is more suicide than murder, than homicide and that it also depends on sex.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness. You also mentioned torture victims and you said that you have a lot of experience in the area of torture, scientifically speaking. My question is the following: Do you know or do you have an occasion to find information in relation to torture that was practised in Sarajevo in that part of Sarajevo that remained under the control of the so-called Presidency forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Objection. Relevance, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your objection is sustained. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you have one minute left.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I will finish. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to finish on two points. Witness, can you tell us very briefly if an analysis, the way that you do them, is it possible to establish the cause of death and here, I am not talking about sniping, but I'm talking about shelling. That is, I take into consideration other projectiles, for instance, shrapnel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Objection, Mr. President, this goes beyond the scope of the expert's report and it's also not included in the Rule 65 ter summary submitted with respect to this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think so. The witness himself spoke about projectiles. He was talking about different things. It was on the basis of this that I'm asking this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just -- all this goes quicker. Can a forensic medical expert establish the cause of death in cases where someone has become the victim of shrapnel caused by shelling?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And this is my very last question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if you, as an expert, do you know whether chemical or mechanographic analysis of projectiles can establish whether these projectiles come from the same object and if they have exploded -- once having exploded?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: If you do find that fragment, then ballistic expert has to carry analysis and he can answer that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, I was speaking about chemical, mechanical, graphic analysis. Do you know if it is scientifically possible to, having conducted all of the above analyses, is it possible to establish whether several fragments come from the same object, from the same shell, for instance, at their origin?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: I did understand the question but ballistic expert, if he -- if projectile fragments are found in the body I can establish the cause of death but then one fragments or several fragments can be passed on to the ballistic expert and then he can establish whether this has come from the same shell or the same projectile.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do I correctly understand you answer that your expertise gives no answer to that question, whereas a ballistic expert might have an answer to that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A ballistic expert must answer that question while I can talk about the cause of death.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I don't think that my question was properly translated. I'll have to -- I would like to reformulate it one more time with your leave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if chemical analysis or mechanographical analysis, those two types of analysis can allow to establish whether certain fragments, shrapnel fragments belonged at their origin to the same shell or to several shells.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just -- may I ask you: Is your knowledge of the technology just mentioned by Defence counsel sufficient to answer the question whether these techniques could allow to establish that different fragments of -- that have been found are originating from the same shell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No doctor can have such knowledge to answer such a question. That is not within the field of the expertise of a doctor, of a medical expert.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You stated a time when doctors knew that everything is over; is that a correct understanding of your answer? We'll adjourn until ten minutes past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, last week, the Prosecution advised the Chamber that we would have an opinion today with respect to the report of the demography expert Dr. Radovanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The time you need to prepare for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, we would object to the tender of that report and would respectfully request four hours for cross-examination of that expert.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And your objections are therefore you -- you don't take the full 30 days then you now have expressed yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mundis. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, although I did not hear you say the words that you had no further questions, I assume that that was just last question before the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I mentioned -- I spoke about my last question, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... Confuse us now and then. Mr. Mundis, are you ready to cross-examine the expert witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Professor Dunjic, you will now be examined by counsel for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, with the assistance of the usher I would ask that the witness be provided with a blank piece of A4 paper, please. Cross-examined by Mr. Mundis:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if you could, I'd like to focus your attention on sniping incident number 4, the one which you discussed at length during your testimony here this afternoon. I would like you to draw a picture of the back, a human back, and indicate the various anatomical parts that are referred to in the medical report associated with sniping incident number 4.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: Just a minute, let me find it. According to the medical documentation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it would be possible for you to make your drawings when the piece of paper is on the ELMO, then we are better able to follow. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the back of a human body according to medical documentation as it has been written down here and that's how I'm going to interpret it. Bullet wound caused entry through the -- an entry wound through the right hemithorax of the back extension of the 5th cervical ring. This is the right hemithorax, if we take this to be part of the diaphragm, we have one shoulder-blade here and the other one here and here we have the right hemithorax. Let's say that it is number five, that these are the last extensions. This is the right hemithorax, point number five and it goes through the left, as it says in the document, upholstery. This would be the direction. If we look at this from above, as I drew it, in order for it to be clear this is the left hand, here we have -- this is the left arm, we have we have the right arm, so the projectile, this is the end of the spine. The projectile goes in this direction and what I said, Mr. President, -- I don't have a detailed description so I can't say whether the projectile goes in this direction or under the skin in this direction, but this is the direction if this is the entry wound, if the entry wound is located here. The position of the body which he described and I drew it here, this was a position of the body and this was the direction from which the projectile came in his opinion or perhaps it was this direction, it doesn't matter so it's all on the left. So here we have sin, left, and dex, right. They're the Latin terms. He had the entry wound here, if you compare it to the image here you can see that the projectile followed this route or it followed this second route according to the description provided to Mr. Prosecutor, so this is how it stands in the description which is why I said in my opinion, in my report, that it's essential for me to determine with precision -- well, if this is the human body, here we have the spine, here we have one shoulder-blade and here we have the other one. It's essential to determine whether the projectile entered the right hemithorax here because this is where the 5th vertebrae is located more or less or did it enter here? So I have the direction according to which it went left, but I don't know whether it descended or whether it ascended and we also have the sloping terrain on which the body was located to given these characteristics of the channel, given both of these routes it's possible to establish where they fired from below or from above in this direction because of the location of the entry wound, the importance of the location of the entry wound and determining the channel wound these are things that I simply can't find here; it's not mentioned. All they mention is the right hemithorax and nothing else, the 5th vertebrae and the left so-called upholstery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, with respect to the testimony of the victim in respect to this incident, in preparing your report, did you read the transcripts of his evidence as provided in the courtroom before the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: That would be it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, it appears the witness is holding the OTP witness statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It looks as if he's showing a witness statement but perhaps could you -- it could not be put on the ELMO, but -- could we just have a look at the document you just pointed at so that -- without having to close the ... When the witness referred to a document while answering the last question, he was referring to a document which bears in bold, "ezava zvedoka" [phoen] which has ERN number 03041180 up till 83 as the last two digits and that's the B/C/S version which appears to be a witness statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, the -- were you shown or provided with one statement of this witness or more than one statement of this witness?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: I have this statement here and I also had the statement that was previously provided on the 11th of November, 1995, the initial statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did either of the statements that you were provided with contain a series of photographs attached to them and which had been marked by the witness?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: I can't see any photographs here now. I examined this carefully, it's -- it's 52379B that's the number of the photograph and the video is 3280AA, that's what I took into consideration that -- as I've said. There aren't any relevant medical documents in my opinion for my report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you recall -- or are you telling us that you do not recall seeing any photographs taken of this victim, you were not provided that by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: No, I don't have any photographs here. I don't have any at the moment. I saw them last time I came, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just -- I just ask for clarification for the sake of the transcript, the transcript reads now in page 72, line 12, 52379B, should that -- did you refer to P3 -- could you please repeat the number exactly of the photographs you mentioned please do it slowly so that we -- you referred to some photographs.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P279B.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I now have on the transcript P279B but I heard a few more is it P3279B? Yes. Thank you. May I just ask for a clarification; are these coloured photographs with apart from that number on it some red numbers on each of the photographs as well? Professor Dunjic, these photographs that you were referring to, are these coloured photographs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have the photographs. I don't have them here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You just mentioned the number that you have written down for yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I wrote them down but I don't have them here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now it's clear to me. Please proceed, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, let me return to the question of transcripts. Did you read or were you shown the transcripts of the victim's testimony when he testified in this courtroom in January of 2002?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: I had a disc. All of it had been recorded on it. I read through it and I saw the transcript.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the transcript at pages 2399 and 2400, the witness indicated - he physically stood up in the courtroom and indicated - the entry and exit wounds that were the result of the bullet that struck him. Do you recall his testimony?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall, as part of reviewing that testimony, that the description of where the bullet entered his body was the spinal region about halfway down his back?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: I have to accept this as a guideline, as the case for all statements, but until I see it, I can't confirm that because that's not how it's described in the medical documents. The documents are important to me and what I see, so seeing the witness, seeing the wound. I believe that he pointed to the wounds in front of me but that's just one piece of information. They have mentioned TH5 in the transcripts so if that's in the vicinity of the 5th vertebrae, it could be at this point and it could be here too but it's not medically relevant to me, if I don't have the opportunity of seeing the wound and if I can't see where the exit wound is located. So that statement is relevant to me just like any other statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I don't know whether the drawings, which are now numerous, the witness' drawings will be tendered or marked for the purpose of identification but if this is the case, it would be good if we could avoid having too many elements because we will completely lose our bearings otherwise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, as a matter of fact, I have been wondering since the witness used some other sketches as well during the examination-in-chief whether there would be a way of perhaps numbering them and the order he used them and I leave it to the parties. It was not quite clear to me whether some of the sketches were just illustrations or whether they were really be needed to tendered into evidence I leave it to the parties but if you intend to tender these sketches in evidence, it should be properly recorded. Mr. Mundis, I leave it up to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if you could return to the picture of the back region, if you could place that on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please assist the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you referring to this one?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe you also indicated without marking other locations which the witness said or could have been referring to when he said or when the description was put forward as being the spinal region about halfway down the back. Did you point to another location on that drawing that's before you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: These two points here, these two points on this trajectory here. It could be either here or here but I didn't see them. If you saw them, if you can say where they were with precision, that's fine, but I didn't. I couldn't see this in his statement because his statement and the medical documents do not agree. The right hemithorax is this part here from the spine to the right and it's near the lungs so the projectile should go like this. I don't know. I have to rely on the witness' statement and the medical documentation. I only read the statement. I didn't see the witness as you did, but these two elements do not correspond to each other, the statement and the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's still some issue that needs to be clarification. You -- is the translation okay or --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said that you had seen the transcripts and you had a disc, I think you said. When you were referring to the transcript, what do you mean exactly by transcript that you -- is that a transcript of the ones you are just referring to or -- because Mr. Mundis was asking you about a transcript of what a witness said in this courtroom and the transcript, I can explain that to you, is where you see question and then you have literally the question and answer and if one of the judges interferes so a literal transcript of what has been said in this court. Did you see such a transcript?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you've told us that you did not see the victim referred to in this incident; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any photographs taken of the injuries that he received?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At any time, did you ask to see any photographs taken of the victim?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: No, or rather I asked to be provided with all the medical documentation that there was, the photographs, the x-rays, et cetera, et cetera. And what I have commented on is what I was provided with, there's nothing else or rather I wasn't provided with anything else. I would be happy to have a look at other documents if there are any.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ask the Defence counsel to provide you with any photographs or to seek to have such photographs taken in the event there weren't any photographs?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately when it was that you first made that request to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: I really don't know. That was when I received the request to carry out the examination to do the report, and when I got the documents that were handed over to me, I saw what was not there, what was missing, and that's -- in that sense, I intervened. I did not receive anything except what I have listed, so it is on the basis of the relevant documents, the photographs, and the video and so on that I gave my opinion because I saw that there was a lot of things that were missing. In each individual case, I saw what was missing and I said, "This was missing," but when that was, I really don't know. That was when I received the request last year to look over this and to do the report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the approximate month or time when you received the request from the Defence?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: Last year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it in December of last year or October of last year or January of last year?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: That was -- just a moment, let me have a look.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in the meantime, could we just check and gain time, perhaps we can have the photograph of ERN number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I think you misunderstood what Mr. Mundis was asking. Could you please first -- you found the date on which the -- you got your request or the month?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] September 2002.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... I did understand, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, but please correct me, Mr. Mundis, if I am wrong that when you asked about possible pictures that would be either existing pictures or pictures still to be taken; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did you ever indicate to the Defence that it would be important for you in compiling your report if you were to undertake an examination of the victim?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately when you made that request?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: When I was doing the report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to return now, Witness, to the testimony of the victim as he gave it in the courtroom. Again, he was asked to indicate, to point on his body where it was the exit wound was located on his body and he indicated the right rear shoulder in the vicinity of his right arm, the top of his right arm. Do you recall seeing that when you read the transcript testimony of this witness?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: Right shoulder, well, I really don't remember right shoulder, here it says the left, so-called upholstery of the thorax area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say it says here the left, you're referring to the medical documentation; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is most relevant for me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'm suggesting to you that the evidence which is most relevant is where the victim actually indicated on his own body where the bullet entered and where the bullet exited. What would your response be to that suggestion?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: Let me tell you from my own experience, I cannot accept that a priori because very often, the person who is hit, they know where they were hit, for instance, in the thoracic area and if it came out the opposite side, for instance in the front, he knows that the projectile exited there and that is a relevant fact for you. But for me, as a forensic expert who has to establish whether this is a projectile, to establish what type of projectile, whether it's a direct hit and which direction in the channel of the injury has, what's relevant to me is what I can see only personally so his statement or his testimony must be corroborated by a medical fact in order to have validity for the Trial Chamber. That is the role of the expert. So it's not just question of establishing the exit and the entry location and the direction of the channel but to see that wound, that area, to see whether it is an exit or an entry wound and what characteristics that scar has. That is what's so important. I have had that in my practice. There is a lot of confusion can occur, particularly if the distances between the entry and the exit wound are very short, the channel is very short. So the person knows they've been hit in the back, but they don't know how the projectile, where it went. For us, for experts it's very important how that projectile went through the body and what it did while it was going through the body.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you recall the position that the victim indicated on the videotape that he was in at the time he was struck by the bullet; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: Yes. And that, for me, is a relevant initial data.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm suggesting to you, witness, that that victim then came into the courtroom and physically indicated on his body that the bullet entered in the spinal region about halfway down his back and exited near the right shoulder in the vicinity of his upper right arm. Would that be consistent --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object. We are in the same line of questioning that was put earlier and the witness has already answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness has given a long answer but not necessarily an answer to the question. Please proceed, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What you are saying here, if that was so, that it was at the level of the fifth thoracic vertebrae and it exited here in the left hemithorax, exited here. Now I'm telling you, can you tell me about the direction of the channel? Does that correspond to the medical --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Professor Dunjic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A question has been put to you. Will you please answer the questions? If the question is, for example, do you agree with me that if the witness testified so that it would be a basis for any further conclusions that it was on the left or in his -- in his leg, then please answer that question and what you are doing very often is to give further explanation about what that all could mean. If Mr. Mundis is interested to know the consequences of your answer, he'll certainly ask for it. Don't be afraid, he will. So would you please listen carefully to the questions, first answer these questions, and if any further information is needed, the parties will certainly ask for it. Please proceed, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, let me try the question again. I'm suggesting that the victim came into the courtroom and physically indicated on his body that the bullet entered in the spinal region about halfway down his back and exited here near the right shoulder in the vicinity of his upper arm. Would that be consistent with the direction to which he pointed and the position he was in in the videotape that you reviewed and which we all looked at earlier this afternoon?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: No. If you're asking me to give an answer as an expert, no, that is not sufficient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Again, the question was not whether it is sufficient, but the question was whether it was consistent with the indication of the direction the witness gave at the video. No one is asking you whether you would draw certain conclusions. The question is whether what has been just indicated to you, whether that would be compatible or incompatible with what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Even that possibility would not be fully compatible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'm suggesting to you that the medical documentation which you reviewed and which relates to this incident was incorrect, the description of the injuries received was incorrect. What is your reaction to that statement?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: If it is incorrect or incorrectly written, then any conclusion can be incorrect. I must, as a medical expert, forensic expert, and all of us who are forensic experts and who operate in this manner, we have to stick to, in such cases, we have to stick to medical documentation. If there is a obvious discrepancy between the medical documentation and this statement or the testimony of the witness which here, in this case, this is the case, as you have said, then absolutely, because of you, it is necessary to have an expert valid opinion. Through an expert report, by examination of such a witness, I can correct the medical documentation, I can say on the left-hand side of the hemithorax there is no scar from a projectile, but there is such a scar in the area of the right shoulder. In that case, through my expert report, I can make the previous medical documentation null and void and I can make this correct version as the witness indicated. Then I can determine, establish the direction of the channel and then I can then put into perspective his own statement if he says where the fire has come from and so on and this is the road to the truth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In light of the fact, Witness, that you've accepted or let me rephrase, do you accept the possibility that the medical report is incorrect?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: Apart from the testimony of the injured person, I don't have any other factual element that could make the medical document null and void except for what you're stating here to me now and what the witness had said in the transcript and demonstrated himself in the courtroom, but I did not see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, again, I would like to ask you if, assuming, assuming for the sake of the argument, the medical report is incorrect, if that were the case, and the victim's injuries were as he described them to the Trial Chamber, I suggest to you that those injuries are consistent with a source of fire being behind him as he indicated in the video that we reviewed.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, if this is true, which I cannot state for certain, because I don't have any factual proof of that, his position of the body at the time of the injury was possibly slightly more at this angle, but let's state like this that the injuries near the spine, this is the front area, and the channel went to the right shoulder, I don't know in which direction it went, so he showed that fire came from here, he exactly showed the position in the case that it is true what the witness stated or rather what you saw and I did not see, that means that fire must have come from these positions here. That is one thing. Another thing, what I do not know, is the following fact: What is the angle from here, is it this angle or this angle or is it horizontal? From that angle, bearing in mind its defined position when he was hit, that depends where the fire came from. We have a counter slope, that is we have a sloping area, sloping ground--

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Professor Dunjic, I know that you really need a lot of information before you come to conclusions as an expert. The question was quite simple that if the statement of the -- the testimony of the witness in this courtroom would reflect the truth whether it is possible that the fire came from the direction he indicated on the videotape or whether there's any reason for which you could say that it is not possible that it came from the direction as indicated on the video. That's the question. I must remind you that you should listen to the question. I am -- there's a lot of very interesting information, you certainly would have, but the first of all, we'd like to have your answer to a specific question. So again, Mr. Mundis has asked you whether, if the description of the wounds as indicated by the witness is correct, whether there would be any reason for you, as an expert, to say that this is incompatible with the direction he indicated on the video. Could you please answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are many reasons why it should be said expertly that it would not correspond to the direction that he showed, and that's the photograph right here. He showed that there was a straight line in relation to his body and now we're talking about the right shoulder where the fire could have come from. So what I'm saying is it does not correspond to what he demonstrated. What he showed, it is not compatible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I note the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it's approximately 7.00. Professor Dunjic, since it might be possible that the parties would like to have your diagrams in evidence, I would ask you to hand them, to start with, all of them, to the registrar. She'll take care that they are still available tomorrow. Would that -- apart from those diagrams.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is this needed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are the bullets and the entrance -- let's just for sake of -- perhaps it's better that you give them as well. There were also some diagrams that you did not make yourself but that were illustrative of what you told us. If you can miss them of course.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I remember that we had pictures of bullet wounds and those, yes. I think the big one you did not show yet but the other one when the -- no, no, only one of that because the other ones have not been shown to us as far as I can see.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the same thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, we've got nine for the price of one, yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, I did not see it go, but there was one document which was in green ink which we were particularly interested in which is where the fire had come from had relation to a vertical view. Thank you very much indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Professor Dunjic, I instruct you not to speak with anyone about the testimony you have given until now and the testimony still about to be given tomorrow. We'll adjourn until tomorrow at quarter past 2.00 in this same courtroom and if there is --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, just one thing before we adjourn I would be grateful if I could have some indication of when the Prosecution could expect the exhibits for the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, that's asked and answered. I don't know why this has to be repeated, but I would also like to have some answers to my last letter that I addressed to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's a good that you want an answer to your letters. The -- perhaps I did not follow it exactly but the question was when the exhibits would be received by the Prosecution. Do I understand your answer that you say that's asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have already given and I can see that the case manager of Mr. Ierace who is nodding her head, I have already given all this and who will give it to Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what I, as a matter of fact, heard you approximately saying in French whereas the English transcript is --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, Mr. Piletta-Zanin informed my case manager during this afternoon's session that first thing tomorrow we will get those exhibits and what I'd like to know is it going to be five minutes or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just ask first because I think it's of no use for you, Professor Dunjic, to spend your time on procedural issues we have to deal with I will just ask the usher to escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. Piletta-Zanin informed our case manager this afternoon that there were some exhibits being photocopied, some cassettes being prepared and we would get them tomorrow. The state of affairs that that is simply not sufficient information given that we are likely to have the next witness shortly after we commence tomorrow's session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand you well that since Mr. Piletta-Zanin indicated that you are to receive it by tomorrow that he should have refrained from comment that you should not ask about it because he had provided already this -- these documents; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then if it is true that you indicated that it would be received by tomorrow and that was even said this afternoon to the case manager, there would have been no reason to give the comment you made, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. What I would suggest, under these circumstances, to you, is to say, as Mr. Ierace might not yet know, we achieved even quicker delivery of these documents not by tomorrow but by today.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I still haven't got my answer to the letter that I had written and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we will discuss that tomorrow. We will adjourn until quarter past 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
